chunks: He said: Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Malik al-Nahwi reported to me, he said: Muhammad ibn al-Fadhl narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Katib narrated to us, he said: Yamoot ibn al-Muzarra’ narrated to us, he said: Isa ibn Ismail narrated to us, from al-Asma’i, who said:

I heard a Bedouin, and he mentioned the rulers, and said: If indeed they have attained honour through injustice in this world, they shall surely be humiliated through justice in the Hereafter. They were content with little instead of much, and with the insignificant instead of the momentous. They shall only encounter ruin at a time when regret will be of no avail.

He said: And Abu al-Hasan recited to me the verses of Abu al-‘Atahiya: Glory to the Master of the Dominion! What a night that laboured forth the dawn of the Day of Standing! If only a soul that is preoccupied with itself could see what is portrayed in the Place of Return, it would not blink — the terrors of annihilation are upon the creation of its Lord. And mankind is divided between those who have gone ahead and those who remain behind.
May Allah bless our master Muhammad the Prophet and his family and grant them peace.

key_terms.السُّلْطَانَ: The rulers; those who hold political power and authority
key_terms.الْمَلَكُوتِ: The Dominion; God’s absolute sovereignty over all creation
key_terms.يَوْمِ الْمَوْقِفِ: The Day of the Standing; the Day of Judgment when all creation stands before God

ai.seo_question: What did al-Asma’i hear a Bedouin say about unjust rulers and the Day of Judgment?
ai.summary: Al-Asma’i, the renowned Arab philologist, heard a Bedouin comment on unjust rulers: though they gain worldly honour through oppression, divine justice will humiliate them in the Hereafter, and their regret will come too late. Abu al-Hasan then recited poetry by Abu al-‘Atahiya describing the awe and terror of the Day of Judgment — if a soul could truly perceive what awaits in the Hereafter, it would be paralysed by fear. The hadith closes with blessings upon the Prophet and his family.
